name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on *all* PRs for one week first. This gives us a full baseline of its impact across the codebase, not just on new contributors. The trade-off is temporary noise in reviews and possible slowdowns, but it’s the only way to measure real-world performance before narrowing scope. After that week, we’ll have data to decide if shadowing only new-contributor PRs is worth the risk of missing edge cases in mature code.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode risks normalizing PR-Agent noise—reviewers will ignore *all* comments if the signal-to-noise ratio is bad. Instead, run it only on PRs from new contributors for two weeks; that gives a clean baseline without polluting veteran reviews. Settle it by measuring reviewer engagement: if comments get ignored in shadow mode, the experiment fails.
